analysis.is_complaint_reason: Customer expresses dissatisfaction that an ISA transfer in took six weeks against a stated 15 working days, and alleges about £56 of lost interest (CH-1).
analysis.summary: Customer reports that an ISA transfer in from another provider took about six weeks, against the 15 working days they were told. They estimate they lost about £56 interest while the transfer was stuck and ask the bank to sort it. Case file records the transfer as received 03/09 and completed 15/10. No vulnerability is recorded. The customer prefers email, and gave a mobile number as an alternative. No actions by the bank are recorded in the case file. The £56 figure is the customer's estimate and has not been verified.

timeline.event: ISA transfer in received from another provider (as written in note)
Customer was told the transfer would take 15 working days
Complaint received by email from customer

analysis.severity_reason: Customer alleges financial loss of about £56 interest, which is under £100 (CH-6 Low). No vulnerability, fraud or repeated contact recorded.

vulnerability.suggested_support: None indicated in the case file. No adjustments required beyond the customer's stated email preference.

analysis.routing_reason: No ESC-1 trigger identified (no fraud, lending, vulnerability referral, systemic issue, legal threat, media contact or systems failure requiring technical investigation). Complaints handler to resolve.

policy_citations.quote: A complaint is any expression of dissatisfaction, oral or written, about the bank's products, services or staff
policy_citations.how_it_applies: Customer is dissatisfied with the time taken for the ISA transfer and alleges financial loss, so this is a complaint.

policy_citations.quote: financial loss under £100 or a service issue with no loss
policy_citations.how_it_applies: Alleged loss of about £56 is under £100, so severity is Low.
The core issue is the delay in completing the ISA transfer, so the primary root cause is Service delay.

policy_citations.quote: Complaints handlers resolve complaints themselves unless one of the following applies
policy_citations.how_it_applies: None of the ESC-1 triggers are identified, so the complaints handler keeps the case.

evidence.quote: my isa transfer from another provider took six weeks
i reckon i lost about £56 interest

handover.complaint_summary: Customer says their ISA transfer in from another provider took about six weeks, though they were told 15 working days. They estimate about £56 interest was lost. Handler to resolve; no specialist trigger identified.
handover.desired_outcome: Customer asks the bank to 'sort it'. No specific remedy or amount stated. Customer's wording: 'can you sort it'.
actions_taken: MISSING: no actions by the bank recorded in the case file
handover.vulnerability_assessment: No vulnerability indicators recorded (note_1: 'no vuln'). Case does not say whether the customer was asked about support needs.
handover.contact_preference: Email (note_1: 'pref email'). Customer also gave a mobile number as an alternative. No reasonable adjustments recorded.
open_questions: How was the £56 interest figure calculated, and over what period?
Where did the 15 working day timescale come from, and who gave it to the customer?
What caused the delay between 03/09 and 15/10?
Has the customer been acknowledged in writing within 3 business days (CH-2)?
Account reference for the ISA is missing from the file.

other_gaps: Interest calculation supporting the £56 figure is not in the case file
No record of acknowledgement sent to customer
analysis.suggested_next_step: Confirm written acknowledgement was sent (CH-2). Verify the transfer dates and the £56 interest claim against the ISA transfer record. Ask the customer for any supporting detail. Decide any redress under CH-8 and RED with an authorised handler; this triage makes no outcome decision.
